notes: The Telegraph Hill Dwellers' Telegraph Hill Bulletin, May 1956 to August 1975 (from March 1967 its masthead reads Telegraph Hill Semaphore): the 56 issues in the Internet Archive collection sanfrancisconewspapers, the forerunner of The Semaphore read in semaphore-1976-1999 and semaphore-2000-2026. 52 of the 56 have no hOCR; text and leaves are rebuilt from each item's _djvu.xml (/mnt/project-files/mission-papers/dl_djvu.py), and citations give the issue month and the leaf. The typed issues of 1956 to 1959 are poorly recognised. Read by hand, with no reader pass: the numbered-address passages, the advertisement-filtered passages (extra_windows.py), and a pass over event words for the places the Bulletin names without a number (kw_scan.py). extra.candidate is the row key in /mnt/project-files/mission-papers/decisions_small2.py. Kept: construction with an architect, demolitions, openings and moves, decisions with an outcome, and documented past occupants (the Rudolph Schaeffer School of Design, Peter Macchiarini's store). Not kept: officers' and members' home addresses, which are most of the numbered addresses in the title; advertisements; meeting places; the Dwellers' positions on the freeway, the waterfront and the height limit; proposals with no outcome; anyone named as the owner of a private house. extra.placement_note says where a number came from when the passage prints none: for 1420 Montgomery, 307 Filbert and 373 Lombard it is the one building on the block that the assessor's roll matches by year and unit count. extra.number_as_printed keeps a printed number filed on a parcel's lowest number.

coverage.remaining: Nothing remains in the Telegraph Hill Bulletin.
coverage.note: 56 issues; 657 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, about 500 of them officers' home addresses and repeating advertisers. 70 passages kept by the filter, 42 more looked at with the advertisement filter off, and 101 event-word passages, all read by hand. 24 findings written, each quote found again in the issue's text. 21 resolved and published on 17 pages (5 seeded: 1420 Montgomery, 307 Filbert, 350 Union, 241 Telegraph Hill Boulevard and 373 Lombard, the last two condominium buildings seeded with their 6 and 17 unit pages). 3 unresolved: the Palace Theater at 1741 Powell, whose building is gone, and two places the Bulletin names without a number (the Sea Wall Warehouse, a Gardner Dailey building at Calhoun and Union). Not carried, the pages having them already: the Peach Blossom Festival at 31 Alta, the Old Spaghetti Factory, the Northeast Mental Health Center's opening at 1548 Stockton, Tel-Hi at 660 Lombard.
